title: Solar System Lagrange Point Dynamics
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates the Sun-Earth-Moon system with all five Sun-Earth Lagrange points (L1–L5) and allows the user to place test particles at those points to observe their orbital stability.

## Scene Setup
- Black background with a starfield of ~200 small white dots.
- A bright yellow emissive sphere for the Sun (radius 8) at the origin.
- A blue sphere for Earth (radius 2) orbiting the Sun at distance 120 in the XZ plane.
- A gray sphere for the Moon (radius 0.6) orbiting Earth at distance 12.
- A PointLight at the Sun position (intensity 2, color 0xffffff) and dim AmbientLight (0x222233).
- Camera starts at (0, 180, 250) looking at origin. Use OrbitControls.
- All orbital motion uses simplified circular Keplerian mechanics. Earth orbital period = 20 seconds real-time. Moon orbital period = 2.5 seconds real-time.

## Lagrange Points
- Compute and display all 5 Sun-Earth Lagrange points as small glowing markers (TorusGeometry, radius 1.5, tube 0.3):
  - L1: between Sun and Earth, ~118 units from Sun along Sun-Earth line.
  - L2: beyond Earth from Sun, ~122 units from Sun along Sun-Earth line.
  - L3: opposite Earth from Sun, ~120 units from Sun on the anti-Earth line.
  - L4: 60 degrees ahead of Earth in its orbit (leading equilateral point).
  - L5: 60 degrees behind Earth in its orbit (trailing equilateral point).
- Lagrange markers co-rotate with Earth (they track the rotating frame).
- Each marker has a label (CSS2DRenderer or sprite) showing 'L1'–'L5'.

## Test Particles
- The user can place a test particle at any Lagrange point by pressing keys 1–5 (places particle at L1–L5 respectively).
- Each placed particle is a small green sphere (radius 0.8). Maximum 5 particles (one per Lagrange point). Pressing the same key again removes that particle (toggle).
- Particles at L4 and L5 should exhibit stable tadpole-like libration (small oscillation around the point). Particles at L1, L2, L3 should slowly drift away (unstable), moving along the Sun-Earth line with exponentially growing displacement over ~10 seconds.
- Track each particle's displacement from its home Lagrange point.

## Simulation Controls
- A DOM button 'Pause/Resume' (id='pauseBtn') toggles simulation time.
- A DOM button 'Reset' (id='resetBtn') removes all particles and resets Earth/Moon to initial angle (0 radians).
- A DOM slider (id='speedSlider', range 0.1 to 5.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controls simulation speed multiplier.
- Keyboard 'R' also triggers reset. Keyboard 'P' also toggles pause.
- A DOM select dropdown (id='viewSelect') with options: 'Inertial Frame', 'Rotating Frame', 'Earth Follow'. In 'Rotating Frame', the camera auto-rotates to keep Earth on the +X axis. In 'Earth Follow', the camera follows behind Earth at offset (0, 30, 40) relative to Earth.

## HUD
- Top-left HUD (id='hud') showing:
  - Simulation time in seconds (id='simTime').
  - Earth orbital angle in degrees (id='earthAngle').
  - Number of active particles (id='particleCount').
  - Current speed multiplier (id='speedDisplay').

## Energy & Conservation
- Track total system pseudo-energy in the rotating frame (Jacobi constant approximation) for each active particle. Display the Jacobi constant of the most recently placed particle (id='jacobiDisplay').
- The Jacobi constant for a stable particle should remain within ±2% of its initial value.

## Undo/Redo
- Pressing 'Z' undoes the last particle placement/removal action. Pressing 'Y' redoes it. Maintain an action history stack (max 20 entries).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- simTime: number (seconds elapsed in simulation)
- paused: boolean
- speedMultiplier: number
- earthAngle: number (radians)
- moonAngle: number (radians)
- lagrangePositions: {L1:{x,y,z}, L2:{x,y,z}, L3:{x,y,z}, L4:{x,y,z}, L5:{x,y,z}}
- activeParticles: {L1:bool, L2:bool, L3:bool, L4:bool, L5:bool}
- particleCount: number
- particleDisplacements: {L1:number|null, L2:number|null, L3:number|null, L4:number|null, L5:number|null} (distance from home Lagrange point)
- jacobiConstants: {L1:number|null, L2:number|null, L3:number|null, L4:number|null, L5:number|null}
- viewMode: string ('Inertial Frame'|'Rotating Frame'|'Earth Follow')
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- earthPosition: {x,y,z}
- sunPosition: {x,y,z}
- frameCount: number (incremented each animation frame)
- totalEnergy: number (sum of all particle Jacobi constants or 0 if none)
physics_constraints: Lagrange points must co-rotate with Earth in the Sun-Earth rotating frame. L1/L2/L3 are collinear (unstable): test particles placed there must drift away with exponentially growing displacement. L4/L5 are equilateral (stable): test particles must exhibit bounded libration. Jacobi constant for each particle must be conserved within ±2% of initial value. Earth orbital radius must remain constant at 120 units. Moon orbital radius must remain constant at 12 units from Earth. All positions must be NaN-free at all times.
